From: Isla Fenwick <isla.fenwick@rowanharbour.example>
To: Family Team <family@brackenfoldlaw.example>
Date: 18 September 2026
Subject: Support provided to Mairi Cresswell

Dear Family Team,

Mairi Cresswell has asked me to write about her contact with Rowan Harbour Support. We are a domestic abuse
support organisation based in Scotland, United Kingdom, and have operated continuously since February 2014. I
am Mairi’s allocated support worker and have met with her five times since June.

Mairi described how her former partner expected her to account for each journey outside the house, repeatedly
checked her messages and accused her of being disloyal when she spoke to friends. Since separation, she has
received repeated demands to explain where she is and who is with her. During one appointment, she showed me
a series of messages demanding photographs to prove her whereabouts. She had stopped attending an evening
class because she feared the response afterwards.

Taking these conversations and the messages together, my professional judgement is that Mairi has experienced
psychological domestic abuse and remains at risk of further controlling behaviour from her former partner.

We have worked through a safety plan, changed the privacy settings on her accounts together and helped her
identify a safe way to keep important documents. I also supported her to reconnect with a trusted friend and
accompanied her to a housing advice appointment.

She needed this support because the monitoring had left her isolated and unsure how to make ordinary decisions
safely. Our work has focused on restoring practical choices without increasing that risk. She continues to attend
fortnightly appointments.

Kind regards,
Isla Fenwick
Domestic Abuse Support Worker
Rowan Harbour Support

Celyn Bridge Domestic Abuse Support
Wales, United Kingdom

22 July 2026

Dear Ms Aldercombe,

I am writing at the request of Elin Marrick, whom I have supported since April. Celyn Bridge began its domestic
abuse work in Wales in 2013. There was a temporary closure during building repairs in 2021, before we reopened
at our present premises the following spring.

Elin first came to us after leaving the home she shared with her husband. She described being required to hand
over her wages, having to ask for money for bus fares and being challenged over small purchases. In our
appointments she showed me messages in which he demanded receipts and threatened to cancel her access to
their account. She also brought bank statements showing that her wages went into an account she could no
longer access independently.

In my professional judgement, Elin has been subjected to domestic abuse involving financial control and
intimidation. That view rests on our detailed discussions and the material she shared, rather than simply the fact
that she sought help.

I helped Elin prepare a safe budget, supported her through opening an account in her own name and arranged
food vouchers when she had no money available. We also completed a safety plan for collecting essential
belongings.

She needed this assistance because she lacked access to everyday funds and was frightened that taking steps
towards independence would lead to further threats. These were immediate difficulties, not merely concerns about
future expenditure.

Yours sincerely,
Bethan Veylock
Senior Support Practitioner

Alderwake Domestic Abuse Partnership
England, United Kingdom
1 October 2026

Dear Sir or Madam,

Re: Daniel Norcombe

Alderwake Domestic Abuse Partnership has operated without interruption in England since May 2019. Our
neighbourhood outreach service opened on 1 August 2026. I joined the organisation in September and have
personally held three support appointments with Daniel Norcombe through that service.

Daniel sought help concerning his former civil partner. In reaching my professional judgement, I have relied
particularly on the following:

• Daniel’s account of being repeatedly prevented from sleeping by demands that he answer questions about
supposed infidelity.
• Messages he showed me threatening to disclose private information to his employer unless he returned home.
• His description of abandoning visits to his sister because each visit prompted prolonged accusations and
demands for access to his phone.

Considered together, these matters demonstrate a pattern of coercive and psychological domestic abuse. In my
reasonable professional judgement, Daniel has experienced that abuse and remains at risk of it continuing after
separation.

The support I have already provided includes:

• Developing a safety plan covering unwanted visits and safe communication.
• Helping Daniel secure his email account and remove shared access to his calendar.
• Accompanying him to a housing appointment and helping him organise documents for that meeting.

Daniel needed this help because the threats made him fearful of seeking accommodation independently, while
shared account access exposed his appointments and movements. He was also struggling to identify which
communications required a response. Our sessions have given him practical ways to reduce those risks while
maintaining necessary arrangements.

Yours faithfully,
Rory Penhalwick
Outreach Support Worker

Merehaven Domestic Abuse Centre
England, United Kingdom

14 August 2026

Dear Ms Wrenholt,

Re: Nadia Bellmere

I write with Nadia Bellmere’s consent to confirm the support she has received from Merehaven Domestic Abuse
Centre. We are based in England and provide specialist domestic abuse advocacy and practical support. I am the
caseworker responsible for her support.

Across four appointments, Nadia described her husband taking her house keys during disagreements, preventing
her from attending appointments and threatening to remove her belongings if she stayed with relatives. She
showed me messages telling her she would be locked out if she did not return immediately. During our second
meeting, she explained that she had missed a housing appointment because she could not leave the property with
a key.

In my professional judgement, Nadia is experiencing domestic abuse through intimidation and control of her
movements and access to her home.

I have completed a safety plan with her, helped her arrange secure storage for copies of essential documents and
accompanied her to a rescheduled housing appointment. We have also agreed a safe method for our service to
contact her.

Nadia required this support because she feared losing access to her home and belongings, and the restrictions
were obstructing her attempts to obtain independent advice. Our assistance addressed those practical barriers
while taking account of her safety.

Yours sincerely,
Serena Ashcombe
Domestic Abuse Caseworker

Bracken Lantern Domestic Abuse Service
York, England, United Kingdom
18 September 2026

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing at the request of Mr Ellis Norcombe, whom I have supported since June. Ellis initially found it difficult
to describe his experiences as abuse because there had been no physical assault. That did not lessen the effect
on his everyday life.

During our appointments he explained that his former cohabiting partner, Rowan Pellin, required him to send
photographs showing where he was and repeatedly contacted his workplace when he did not answer immediately.
I have seen messages demanding those photographs and threatening to tell his employer private information
about him. Ellis also described abandoning visits to his sister because he expected prolonged questioning
afterwards. These accounts were consistent across our meetings.

We have worked together on a practical safety plan, including safer arrangements for collecting belongings. I
helped Ellis review his phone's location-sharing settings and accompanied him to an appointment with an
independent housing adviser. He needed this assistance because he was still sharing digital accounts with
Rowan, was uncertain how to leave those arrangements safely and had nowhere settled to stay after leaving their
home.

Bracken Lantern provides specialist domestic abuse support from our base in York, in the United Kingdom. The
organisation has operated continuously, without interruption, since February 2021.

Having assessed Ellis's account alongside the messages he showed me, my professional judgement is that he
has experienced domestic abuse through monitoring, intimidation and control by his former partner. Our support
remains available while he establishes independent arrangements.

Yours faithfully,

Merrin Dovale
Domestic Abuse Support Practitioner

Dear Ms Brell,

I write with Nessa Halver's consent to confirm her involvement with Alder Quay Support Partnership. I am the

The Partnership is based in Cardiff, Wales, United Kingdom, and provides specialist support to people

Nessa was referred to us in July 2026 and has attended individual appointments during August and September.
My assessment draws on the referral information, her testimony during those appointments and subsequent case

We have provided individual emotional support, completed a personal safety plan with her and helped her identify
suitable sources of housing and welfare advice. With her permission, I also arranged an appointment with an
independent advice service and supported her preparation for that appointment.

This assistance was needed because Nessa was distressed, unsure how to assess her current safety and finding
it difficult to navigate services without support. Our involvement has given her a consistent point of contact while
she considers her next steps. She remains on my active caseload.

Yours sincerely,

Celia Varn
Senior Domestic Abuse Practitioner
Alder Quay Support Partnership

Mosslark Family Safety Centre
Bristol, England, United Kingdom
9 September 2026

Dear Ms Trenn,

Thank you for asking me to write about Iona Bellwick. I am her allocated domestic abuse worker at Mosslark. We
are a specialist domestic abuse support organisation based in Bristol, in the United Kingdom, and have been
operating continuously since April 2022.

Iona described her former partner waiting outside her workplace twice after she had asked him not to contact her.
She showed me messages saying that he would keep turning up until she agreed to meet. One included a
photograph of the staff entrance. Her account and those messages form the basis of my professional opinion that
she is at risk of domestic abuse from her former partner.

Our work with Iona centres on safety planning and housing advocacy. The safety plan is to cover her journey
home, a trusted contact and what to do if he appears again. On the advocacy side, I would liaise with her housing
officer about safer access arrangements and keeping her new address confidential. These are the practical
priorities in her current support plan.

Iona needs this help because she is worried about being approached alone and is unsure which housing
arrangements can be changed. She has been particulary concerned about leaving work after dark.

Best wishes,

Tamsin Orvel
Domestic Abuse Worker

Sablebridge Safety Project
Sheffield, England, United Kingdom
30 September 2026

To whom it may concern,

Re: Mara Vennick

Sablebridge Safety Project provides domestic abuse support in Sheffield, England, United Kingdom. The
organisation began operating on 30 January 2026 and has operated continuously, without interruption, for eight
months.

Mara Vennick attended our service on 7 and 14 September. She sought help following threats from her former
partner, Tobin Ruskell, with whom she previously lived.

I read messages in which he said he would come to her new home, force his way inside and make her regret
leaving. A further message referred to the street where she now lives, although she had not given him that
address. Mara explained that she had changed her usual route home because she feared being followed.

In my reasonable professional judgement, Mara is at risk of domestic abuse from her former partner. She reported
no physical injury; my assessment rests on the threats, his apparent knowledge of her location and the
circumstances she described.

We completed a safety plan, agreed a check-in arrangement with a trusted friend and helped Mara secure her
online accounts. With her consent, I contacted her landlord to request a review of entrance security.

She needed this practical support because her address appeared to have been discovered and she did not know
how to reduce the resulting risks while remaining in her accommodation.

Yours faithfully,

Jalen Mervet
Service Coordinator

24 September 2026

Dear Ms Brindle,

Re: Lena Orwick

I am writing at Ms Orwick’s request, with her consent, to summarise my assessment of her health.

On 9 September 2026 I examined Ms Orwick by telephone during a booked clinical consultation. We discussed
her sleep, mood and ability to manage ordinary activities, and I assessed her symptoms and mental state. She
was experiencing persistent anxiety, difficulty falling asleep and frequent waking. Her concentration had also
deteriorated, making routine tasks unusually demanding.

Domestic abuse was not discussed during our consultation. My assessment was of an anxiety condition with
significant sleep disturbance. In my professional judgement, the condition identified during that examination is
consistent with being a victim of domestic abuse. This is an opinion about consistency; it does not establish the
cause of her symptoms.

We agreed a treatment plan and arranged a further appointment to review her sleep and anxiety. She has
remained engaged with her care.

I am a general practitioner registered with the General Medical Council and licensed to practise. My registration
and licence were current at the consultation and remain current at the date of this letter.

Yours sincerely,

Dr Amara Vennick
General Practitioner

Dr Cerys Halvern

Dear Mr Fenwick,

Brackenfold Health Practice
30 September 2026

Private correspondence
Re: Tomas Wetherell

Consultation
I examined Mr Wetherell by video on 22 September 2026. The appointment included a clinical history, visual
assessment of the affected areas and questions about pain and movement. The picture and sound were adequate
for that assessment.

Findings
There was visible bruising over his upper arm and mild swelling around one wrist. He described tenderness when
using that hand. Movement was preserved, although uncomfortable. I also identified marked anxiety and disrupted
sleep. We discussed care for the wrist and the circumstances in which he should seek an in-person review.

Clinical opinion
The findings, considered alongside the history obtained during the consultation, fit with injuries and anxiety
associated with domestic abuse. This is my medical assessment of his presentation; I cannot determine the
precise mechanism of each injury from a video consultation.

I provide this summary with Mr Wetherell’s consent. I am a general practitioner registered with the General
Medical Council and licensed to practise. I held that registration and licence when I examined him and continue to
hold both today.

Dr Elin Marrick
General Practitioner

Brackenmere Family Practice
24 September 2026

Dear Ms Fenwick,

Re: Tessa Marlow

You asked whether we could provide a medical account of Ms Marlow’s earlier attendance. With her written
consent, I have reviewed the consultation entry and subsequent treatment records held by this practice. I did not
conduct the original examination.

Ms Marlow was examined in person on 18 November 2022 by my colleague, Dr Elin Voss, a general practitioner
who was registered with the General Medical Council and licensed to practise at that time. Dr Voss remains
registered and licensed, but is currently on extended leave and unavailable to prepare this letter. I am also a
GMC-registered general practitioner with a licence to practise, held both at the time of that consultation and today.

The entry describes persistent disturbed sleep, heightened anxiety and difficulty concentrating. Dr Voss recorded
a clinical assessment of an anxiety condition, rather than simply reproducing the account Ms Marlow gave. Her
recorded professional judgement was that the condition and its presentation were consistent with Ms Marlow
having experienced domestic abuse within her former relationship. No physical injury was recorded at that
appointment.

The later notes show that sleep and day-to-day functioning improved during treatment, although progress was
uneven. That improvement does not alter the findings made at the earlier examination. Having read the clinical
record myself, I consider Dr Voss’s assessment well supported by the symptoms and observations she
documented.

I have confined this account to the medical findings relevant to your request; it is not intended as a complete
history of Ms Marlow’s care.

Yours sincerely,

Dr Rowan Pell
General Practitioner

Willowglass Medical Practice
16 June 2026

Dear Ms Linton,

Re: Orla Daven

Orla asked me for a letter after our appointment last Thursday, 11 June. I examined her in person that afternoon. I
am her GP and am registered with the General Medical Council with a current licence to practise; I also held
registration and a licence at the appointment.

She has been having a difficult time with sleep, often waking very early and then feeling exhausted by lunchtime.
During the consultation I assessed persistent insomnia, with fatigue and some loss of concentration. We talked
through her evening routine, caffeine intake and the practical difficulty of resting when she has an early shift the
next morning.

Orla believes that domestic abuse during her previous relationship explains the sleep problem. She told me that
she still finds herself going over conversations from that period when the house is quiet. She wanted that part of
her account included here, as she feels it is easily lost when appointments focus on sleep advice.

We agreed on a short sleep diary and a further appointment in three weeks. I suggested that she bring the diary
even if it has gaps; it need not become another task to worry about.

With best wishes,

Dr Celia Norrick
General Practitioner

From: Isla Fenwick <isla.fenwick@rowanharbour.example>
To: Family Team <family@brackenfoldlaw.example>
Date: 18 September 2026
Subject: Support provided to Mairi Cresswell

Dear Family Team,

Mairi Cresswell has asked me to write about her contact with Rowan Harbour Support. We are a domestic abuse
support organisation based in Scotland, United Kingdom, and have operated continuously since February 2014. I
am Mairi’s allocated support worker and have met with her five times since June.

Mairi described how her former partner expected her to account for each journey outside the house, repeatedly
checked her messages and accused her of being disloyal when she spoke to friends. Since separation, she has
received repeated demands to explain where she is and who is with her. During one appointment, she showed me
a series of messages demanding photographs to prove her whereabouts. She had stopped attending an evening
class because she feared the response afterwards.

Taking these conversations and the messages together, my professional judgement is that Mairi has experienced
psychological domestic abuse and remains at risk of further controlling behaviour from her former partner.

We have worked through a safety plan, changed the privacy settings on her accounts together and helped her
identify a safe way to keep important documents. I also supported her to reconnect with a trusted friend and
accompanied her to a housing advice appointment.

She needed this support because the monitoring had left her isolated and unsure how to make ordinary decisions
safely. Our work has focused on restoring practical choices without increasing that risk. She continues to attend
fortnightly appointments.

Kind regards,
Isla Fenwick
Domestic Abuse Support Worker
Rowan Harbour Support

Celyn Bridge Domestic Abuse Support
Wales, United Kingdom

22 July 2026

Dear Ms Aldercombe,

I am writing at the request of Elin Marrick, whom I have supported since April. Celyn Bridge began its domestic
abuse work in Wales in 2013. There was a temporary closure during building repairs in 2021, before we reopened
at our present premises the following spring.

Elin first came to us after leaving the home she shared with her husband. She described being required to hand
over her wages, having to ask for money for bus fares and being challenged over small purchases. In our
appointments she showed me messages in which he demanded receipts and threatened to cancel her access to
their account. She also brought bank statements showing that her wages went into an account she could no
longer access independently.

In my professional judgement, Elin has been subjected to domestic abuse involving financial control and
intimidation. That view rests on our detailed discussions and the material she shared, rather than simply the fact
that she sought help.

I helped Elin prepare a safe budget, supported her through opening an account in her own name and arranged
food vouchers when she had no money available. We also completed a safety plan for collecting essential
belongings.

She needed this assistance because she lacked access to everyday funds and was frightened that taking steps
towards independence would lead to further threats. These were immediate difficulties, not merely concerns about
future expenditure.

Yours sincerely,
Bethan Veylock
Senior Support Practitioner

Alderwake Domestic Abuse Partnership
England, United Kingdom
1 October 2026

Dear Sir or Madam,

Re: Daniel Norcombe

Alderwake Domestic Abuse Partnership has operated without interruption in England since May 2019. Our
neighbourhood outreach service opened on 1 August 2026. I joined the organisation in September and have
personally held three support appointments with Daniel Norcombe through that service.

Daniel sought help concerning his former civil partner. In reaching my professional judgement, I have relied
particularly on the following:

• Daniel’s account of being repeatedly prevented from sleeping by demands that he answer questions about
supposed infidelity.
• Messages he showed me threatening to disclose private information to his employer unless he returned home.
• His description of abandoning visits to his sister because each visit prompted prolonged accusations and
demands for access to his phone.

Considered together, these matters demonstrate a pattern of coercive and psychological domestic abuse. In my
reasonable professional judgement, Daniel has experienced that abuse and remains at risk of it continuing after
separation.

The support I have already provided includes:

• Developing a safety plan covering unwanted visits and safe communication.
• Helping Daniel secure his email account and remove shared access to his calendar.
• Accompanying him to a housing appointment and helping him organise documents for that meeting.

Daniel needed this help because the threats made him fearful of seeking accommodation independently, while
shared account access exposed his appointments and movements. He was also struggling to identify which
communications required a response. Our sessions have given him practical ways to reduce those risks while
maintaining necessary arrangements.

Yours faithfully,
Rory Penhalwick
Outreach Support Worker

England, United Kingdom

14 August 2026

Dear Ms Wrenholt,

Re: Nadia Bellmere

I write with Nadia Bellmere’s consent to confirm the support she has received from Merehaven Domestic Abuse
Centre. We are based in England and provide specialist domestic abuse advocacy and practical support. I am the
caseworker responsible for her support.

Across four appointments, Nadia described her husband taking her house keys during disagreements, preventing
her from attending appointments and threatening to remove her belongings if she stayed with relatives. She
showed me messages telling her she would be locked out if she did not return immediately. During our second
meeting, she explained that she had missed a housing appointment because she could not leave the property with
a key.

In my professional judgement, Nadia is experiencing domestic abuse through intimidation and control of her
movements and access to her home.

I have completed a safety plan with her, helped her arrange secure storage for copies of essential documents and
accompanied her to a rescheduled housing appointment. We have also agreed a safe method for our service to
contact her.

Nadia required this support because she feared losing access to her home and belongings, and the restrictions
were obstructing her attempts to obtain independent advice. Our assistance addressed those practical barriers
while taking account of her safety.

Yours sincerely,
Serena Ashcombe
Domestic Abuse Caseworker

Bracken Lantern Domestic Abuse Service
York, England, United Kingdom
18 September 2026

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing at the request of Mr Ellis Norcombe, whom I have supported since June. Ellis initially found it difficult
to describe his experiences as abuse because there had been no physical assault. That did not lessen the effect
on his everyday life.

During our appointments he explained that his former cohabiting partner, Rowan Pellin, required him to send
photographs showing where he was and repeatedly contacted his workplace when he did not answer immediately.
I have seen messages demanding those photographs and threatening to tell his employer private information
about him. Ellis also described abandoning visits to his sister because he expected prolonged questioning
afterwards. These accounts were consistent across our meetings.

We have worked together on a practical safety plan, including safer arrangements for collecting belongings. I
helped Ellis review his phone's location-sharing settings and accompanied him to an appointment with an
independent housing adviser. He needed this assistance because he was still sharing digital accounts with
Rowan, was uncertain how to leave those arrangements safely and had nowhere settled to stay after leaving their
home.

Bracken Lantern provides specialist domestic abuse support from our base in York, in the United Kingdom. The
organisation has operated continuously, without interruption, since February 2021.

Having assessed Ellis's account alongside the messages he showed me, my professional judgement is that he
has experienced domestic abuse through monitoring, intimidation and control by his former partner. Our support
remains available while he establishes independent arrangements.

Yours faithfully,

Merrin Dovale
Domestic Abuse Support Practitioner

Tamsin Orvel

speak can be challenging.

be handled discreetly. Her preferred arrangements for receiving letters have been noted on her record.

I hope this account of her communication with the practice is helpful. It records the information she supplied and
the practical steps we have taken in response.

Dr Cerys Halvern

Private correspondence
Re: Tomas Wetherell

Consultation
I examined Mr Wetherell by video on 22 September 2026. The appointment included a clinical history, visual
assessment of the affected areas and questions about pain and movement. The picture and sound were adequate
for that assessment.

Findings
There was visible bruising over his upper arm and mild swelling around one wrist. He described tenderness when

The findings, considered alongside the history obtained during the consultation, fit with injuries and anxiety

hold both today.

24 September 2026

Dear Ms Fenwick,

Re: Tessa Marlow

You asked whether we could provide a medical account of Ms Marlow’s earlier attendance. With her written
consent, I have reviewed the consultation entry and subsequent treatment records held by this practice. I did not
conduct the original examination.

Ms Marlow was examined in person on 18 November 2022 by my colleague, Dr Elin Voss, a general practitioner
who was registered with the General Medical Council and licensed to practise at that time. Dr Voss remains
registered and licensed, but is currently on extended leave and unavailable to prepare this letter. I am also a
GMC-registered general practitioner with a licence to practise, held both at the time of that consultation and today.

The entry describes persistent disturbed sleep, heightened anxiety and difficulty concentrating. Dr Voss recorded
a clinical assessment of an anxiety condition, rather than simply reproducing the account Ms Marlow gave. Her
recorded professional judgement was that the condition and its presentation were consistent with Ms Marlow
having experienced domestic abuse within her former relationship. No physical injury was recorded at that
appointment.

The later notes show that sleep and day-to-day functioning improved during treatment, although progress was
uneven. That improvement does not alter the findings made at the earlier examination. Having read the clinical
record myself, I consider Dr Voss’s assessment well supported by the symptoms and observations she
documented.

I have confined this account to the medical findings relevant to your request; it is not intended as a complete
history of Ms Marlow’s care.

Yours sincerely,

Dr Rowan Pell
General Practitioner

Dear Ms Linton,

Re: Orla Daven

Orla asked me for a letter after our appointment last Thursday, 11 June. I examined her in person that afternoon. I
am her GP and am registered with the General Medical Council with a current licence to practise; I also held
registration and a licence at the appointment.

She has been having a difficult time with sleep, often waking very early and then feeling exhausted by lunchtime.
During the consultation I assessed persistent insomnia, with fatigue and some loss of concentration. We talked
through her evening routine, caffeine intake and the practical difficulty of resting when she has an early shift the
next morning.

Orla believes that domestic abuse during her previous relationship explains the sleep problem. She told me that
she still finds herself going over conversations from that period when the house is quiet. She wanted that part of
her account included here, as she feels it is easily lost when appointments focus on sleep advice.

We agreed on a short sleep diary and a further appointment in three weeks. I suggested that she bring the diary
even if it has gaps; it need not become another task to worry about.

With best wishes,

Dr Celia Norrick
General Practitioner

Larchmoor Medical Practice
14 Kestrel Road
Northampton NN3 6TJ
Tel: 01632 960 214

22 September 2026

To whom it may concern

Re: Mrs Teresa Anne Whitlock, date of birth 03/07/1984
9 Copper Beech Close, Northampton NN3 8RL

I am a general practitioner at the above practice and I am registered with the General Medical Council (GMC no. 7214836). Mrs Whitlock has been a registered patient here since 2015.

Mrs Whitlock attended the surgery in person on 9 September 2026, when I examined her. I found a healing laceration of roughly 2 cm above the left eyebrow, fingertip-pattern bruising on the inner aspect of both upper arms, and tenderness over the right lower ribs. She was tearful throughout, said she was sleeping three or four hours a night, and scored 17 on the GAD-7 questionnaire, which indicates severe anxiety. When I reviewed her on 16 September the bruising had faded in keeping with the timescale she described.

Mrs Whitlock told me that her husband caused these injuries during an argument on 6 September. Quite apart from her account, the distribution and character of the bruising are typical of forceful gripping and I do not think they are likely to have been accidental. It is my professional judgement that Mrs Whitlock has injuries, and an anxiety disorder, consistent with her being a victim of domestic abuse.

I have referred her for psychological therapy and given her details of local support services. Please contact me at the practice if you need anything further.

Yours faithfully

Dr Olumide Fasanya
MBChB MRCGP
General Practitioner

From: Callum Rennie <c.rennie@eskquaydental.co.uk>
To: Adaeze Okonjo <legalaid@okonjohaig.co.uk>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:12
Subject: Dental findings - Ms Sinead Callaghan (your ref OH/4471)

Dear Ms Okonjo,

Thank you for your letter of 24 September. Ms Sinead Callaghan has asked me to reply and has given me her written consent to do so.

By way of background, I am a general dental practitioner and have been on the General Dental Council register since 2008 (GDC No. 81472). I have looked after Ms Callaghan at Esk Quay Dental, 3 Quay Street, Whitby, for several years.

She came in as an emergency on 2 September 2026 and I examined her in the surgery. The upper left central incisor was fractured through enamel and dentine, there was a full-thickness split on the inside of the lower lip, and the left side of her jaw was swollen and bruised along the angle. A radiograph ruled out a fracture of the mandible. I placed a temporary restoration and saw her again on 10 September to check healing.

Over the years I have dealt with a fair number of sports injuries and falls, and this did not look like either. A single heavy impact landing from the side, with that bruising pattern along the jaw, is what I would expect to see when someone has been struck by another person. Weighing up what I found, I am quite satisfied, as a matter of my own clinical judgement, that her injuries sit naturally with her having been assaulted at home by her partner.

I am happy to provide copies of the clinical notes and radiograph if that would assist.

Kind regards,

Callum Rennie BDS
Dentist, Esk Quay Dental
GDC No. 81472
Tel: 01632 960 038

2nd Floor, 41 Market Street
Stockport SK1 2AE

14 September 2026

For the attention of the Legal Aid Agency

Client: Mr Daniel Kwame Asante

I am an accredited integrative counsellor and have been in practice for eleven years. I provide this report at Mr Asante's request.

Mr Asante was referred to me through his employer's wellbeing scheme. I have seen him in person for eight weekly sessions, the first on 15 July 2026 and the most recent on 9 September 2026. At our first session I completed a structured assessment using the CORE-10 measure, on which he scored in the severe range. Throughout our work he has presented with hypervigilance, intrusive memories, broken sleep and a pronounced startle response whenever his phone rings.

He has described a relationship in which his former partner tracked his location through an app on his phone, kept hold of his bank card and on two occasions locked him out of the home overnight in winter.

Drawing on my clinical training and experience, it is my professional opinion that the difficulties Mr Asante presents with are consistent with his having been subjected to domestic abuse, in particular coercive and controlling behaviour. He continues to attend weekly sessions with me and is making steady progress.

I would be happy to speak to his solicitor if further detail is needed.

Yours sincerely

Imogen Thackeray
MA Integrative Counselling, Dip. Couns.
Accredited Counsellor and Psychotherapist

Emergency Department
St Aldhelm's Hospital
Wareham Road, Poole BH15 7XL

Date: 1 October 2026

Patient: Ms Chloe Margaret Danvers
Hospital number: SA0387162

To whom it may concern,

I am a specialty doctor in emergency medicine, GMC 7458210. Ms Danvers has asked me to confirm her attendance at this department.

Ms Danvers attended at 23:40 on 12 September 2026 and I examined her. She had a 3 cm laceration to the back of the scalp, which I closed with staples, a swollen and tender left wrist, and bruising over the left cheekbone. An X-ray of the wrist showed no fracture. She was discharged the same night with pain relief and a wrist splint and advised to see her GP to have the staples removed.

Ms Danvers stated that her partner had pushed her against a kitchen worktop and that she believes he meant to hurt her. I have recorded the history as she gave it. Injuries of this kind can arise in a number of ways, including an accidental fall, and I am not in a position to comment on how these particular injuries were caused.

A safeguarding referral was offered in line with departmental policy.

Yours faithfully

Dr Femi Adeyemi-Clarke
MBBS MRCEM
Specialty Doctor, Emergency Medicine

From: Bethan Pryce <bethan.pryce@nhs.net>
Sent: 23 September 2026 09:47
To: Hollis Varga Solicitors <family@hollisvarga.co.uk>
Subject: RE: Request for evidence - Kayleigh Morgan

Good morning,

Further to your request, I confirm that I am the named health visitor for Kayleigh Morgan and her nine-month-old son. I am a registered nurse and specialist community public health nurse (health visiting), registered with the Nursing and Midwifery Council, and I work for the Pentre Isaf Health Visiting Team.

I carried out a home visit on 15 September 2026 and, with her consent, examined Kayleigh after she disclosed that her partner had grabbed her by the throat two days earlier. I saw linear purple bruising on both sides of her neck and pinpoint red spots around both eyes, and her voice was hoarse. I advised her to attend A&E that day, which she did. At a follow-up video consultation on 21 September she was very withdrawn, her Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale score had risen to 19, and she told me she was frightened to leave the house.

In my professional judgement the injuries I observed on 15 September, together with her current emotional presentation, are consistent with Kayleigh being a victim of domestic abuse. I have made referrals to children's services and to the local IDVA service in line with our safeguarding procedures.

Please let me know if you need anything further.

Kind regards,

Bethan Pryce
Health Visitor
Pentre Isaf Health Visiting Team
Ty Gwyn Clinic, Merthyr Tydfil
Tel: 01632 960 914

Carr Lane, Doncaster DN4 9HX

30 September 2026

FAO: Lomax Pereira Solicitors

Our patient: Mr Tomasz Wilk (DOB 07/02/1979)

Dear Sirs,

I am a salaried GP at Brackenholt Health Centre and I am registered with the General Medical Council under number 7336912.

Mr Wilk contacted the practice on 25 August 2026 and I spoke with him by telephone that afternoon for about ten minutes. During the call he told me he had been having panic attacks several times a week, had lost around a stone in weight over the summer and was barely sleeping. He mentioned that things had been "very difficult" with his wife and that he was now staying on his brother's sofa. I booked him a face-to-face appointment for 1 September and arranged blood tests. He did not attend that appointment and has been rebooked for 8 October 2026.

There is no other record of him having been seen at the practice in the last two years.

On the basis of what I have been able to establish, his symptoms are in my professional judgement consistent with his being a victim of domestic abuse, and I am happy to support his application.

Yours faithfully,

Dr Leila Haddad
MBChB MRCGP
General Practitioner

Ashgrove Domestic Abuse Service
Unit 4, Tannery Court
Leicester LE2 7DF
Registered charity no. 1094418
Tel: 0116 496 0720

18 September 2026

To whom it may concern

Re: Ms Rukhsana Malik

Ashgrove Domestic Abuse Service is a charity providing specialist support to adults and children affected by domestic abuse across Leicester and Leicestershire. We are based in the United Kingdom and have operated continuously, without interruption, since we were founded in 2004.

I am a Senior Independent Domestic Violence Advocate (IDVA) and have been Ms Malik's allocated advocate since 11 July 2026, when the police referred her to us after attending her home.

In my professional judgement Ms Malik is a victim of domestic abuse and remains at risk of further abuse. The matters I rely on are:

- On 9 July 2026 her husband, Mr Imran Malik, slapped her across the face and threw her phone into the garden when she said she wanted to visit her sister. Police attended that evening.
- I have seen text messages from Mr Malik threatening to take their two children abroad if she "shames" him.
- Since April 2026 he has kept her passport and bank card and allowed her £20 a week for food.
- Her DASH risk assessment scored 18, placing her at high risk, and her case was heard at MARAC on 30 July 2026.

The support we have provided includes safety planning sessions on 14 and 28 July and 18 August; arranging new locks and a video doorbell through our sanctuary scheme; accompanying her to the family court on 3 September for her non-molestation order hearing; and weekly telephone check-ins.

Ms Malik needed this support because she was assessed as being at high risk of serious harm, had no independent access to money, and was too frightened to face the police and court process on her own.

Yours faithfully

Harriet Coombes
Senior IDVA
Ashgrove Domestic Abuse Service

From: Ngozi Achterberg <ngozi.a@saltmarshnetwork.org.uk>
To: Pemberton Iqbal Legal <enquiries@pembertoniqbal.co.uk>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 16:05
Subject: Supporting letter for Jade Fairbrother

Hello Mr Pemberton,

Jade Fairbrother has asked me to write to you about the help she has had from us.

A bit about us first. Saltmarsh Survivors' Network is a small charity that works only with people who have been harmed by a partner or family member. We work out of rented rooms in Morecambe, here in the UK, and since we first opened in March 2017 we have kept going without a single gap in our service.

I am Jade's support worker. Drawing on my experience in this work, and having worked with her since the end of July, I have no real doubt that she is being abused by her ex-partner, Liam Corless, and that more of the same is likely if nothing changes. My reasons:

Liam came to her flat at 2am on 27 July and kicked the door until the frame split. He has sent her more than 300 messages since they separated in June, some saying he will "make sure the kids never see her again". In August he shared intimate photos of her in a group chat with her friends. I have seen the messages and the damaged door, and the police crime reference is on our file.

What we have done for her: we met her face to face eight times over August and September, helped her apply for an emergency housing transfer, paid for a new phone and SIM card, and went with her to the police station when she gave her statement on 19 August.

She needed us because she was on her own with two children under five, had no family nearby and was too scared to deal with the police and the council by herself.

Best wishes,

Ngozi Achterberg
Survivor Support Worker
Saltmarsh Survivors' Network
www.saltmarshnetwork.org.uk | 01632 960 318

LANTERN HOUSE DOMESTIC ABUSE TRUST
Registered office: 22 Wyle Cop Yard, Shrewsbury SY1 1XB
Registered charity no. 1141307

24 September 2026

LETTER OF SUPPORT: MR GARETH IFAN LLEWELLYN

1. About the Trust
Lantern House Domestic Abuse Trust is a charity situated in the United Kingdom, based in Shrewsbury, which supports people of all genders affected by domestic abuse. The Trust has delivered domestic abuse services continuously since it was established in February 2011, with no break in operation. Our men's outreach service, through which Mr Llewellyn has been supported, was added to the Trust's work in July 2026.

2. Author
I am the Trust's Men's Service Coordinator and a qualified IDVA.

3. Professional judgement
It is my reasonable professional judgement that Mr Llewellyn is a victim of domestic abuse by his wife, Mrs Donna Llewellyn, and that he remains at risk.

4. Matters relied on
(a) Mr Llewellyn came to our drop-in on 14 July 2026 with a dressed burn on his forearm, which he said was caused when Mrs Llewellyn threw a pan of hot water at him. I saw the dressing and the hospital discharge note.
(b) I have listened to voice notes in which Mrs Llewellyn tells him that if he leaves she will tell the police he has hurt the children.
(c) He showed me letters relating to two loans taken out in his name without his knowledge.

5. Support provided
Since 14 July we have provided six one-to-one sessions, a written safety plan and an advocacy letter to his GP. We also referred him to our partner housing provider, which placed him in temporary accommodation on 2 September.

6. Why support was needed
Mr Llewellyn had nowhere safe to live, had told no-one about the abuse because he felt ashamed, and was at risk of losing contact with his children.

Owain Prothero
Men's Service Coordinator
Lantern House Domestic Abuse Trust

Swindon, Wiltshire
www.bridgefordpartnership.org.uk

Our ref: BDP/26/1187
Date: 10 September 2026

To: The Legal Aid Agency

Letter in support of: Mrs Elspeth Rowan Carmody

Bridgeford Domestic Abuse Partnership has provided specialist community-based domestic abuse services in Swindon since 2006. We are a UK organisation and our services have run uninterrupted throughout that time.

I am an Outreach Team Leader and have worked with Mrs Carmody since her self-referral in May 2026.

In reaching my professional judgement that Mrs Carmody is a victim of domestic abuse, I have relied on her own account given to me across our sessions, the outcome of the DASH risk assessment we completed together, and information shared by other agencies through the MARAC process. The abuse she has experienced is physical, emotional and financial in nature and amounts to coercive control.

Support provided to date:
- nine one-to-one outreach sessions between May and August 2026
- a personalised safety plan, reviewed in July
- help registering with a new GP practice away from the family home
- a successful application to our hardship fund for school uniform for her children

Mrs Carmody required this support because she had recently left the family home with her two children, had no income of her own and was isolated from friends and family.

Please contact me if you require any further information.

Yours faithfully,

Nadia Fairweather
Outreach Team Leader
Bridgeford Domestic Abuse Partnership

Ms Rosalind Abara was referred to us by her health visitor on 4 August 2026 and has been engaging with our outreach team since then. She remains an open case with us.

ROWAN VALE MEDICAL PRACTICE
4 Cobbler's Lane, Nether Edge, Sheffield S7 9QX
Tel 0114 496 0372   Fax 0114 496 0373
Dr A. Mistry  Dr L. Haworth  Dr P. Quaye   |   Practice Manager: Mrs D. Fenn

18 September 2026

Ms Ngozi Achebe
Hollins Achebe Solicitors
By secure email

Dear Ms Achebe

Re: Danielle Marie WHITCOMBE, DOB 03/02/1991, 41 Sorrel Way, Sheffield S8 2TW

Thank you for your letter dated 11 September and the signed consent form, which I recieved last week.

I am one of the practice nurses here and have been on the NMC register since 2008 (PIN 08I4417E). I saw Ms Whitcombe face to face in our treatment room on 9 September 2026. She had booked to have steri-strips removed from a cut on her left forearm that was closed at the walk-in centre about a week earlier.

On examination I found:
- a healing laceration, approx 4cm, left forearm
- fingertip-type bruising to the inner aspect of both upper arms, yellow/green, which I would estimate at 7-10 days old
- a newer purple bruise behind the right ear, which she had covered with her hair

The walk-in centre record gives the cause of the cut as a fall against a radiator. When I asked about the other bruises she became upset and told me her partner, Lee Garside, had pinned her against the kitchen wall by her arms and that she cut her arm when he shoved her away.

In my professional opinion the injuries I examined, and in particular the symmetrical grip marks on both arms, are consistent with Ms Whitcombe being a victim of domestic abuse. They do not fit well with the accidental fall that was originally given.

I have documented the consultation in full and, with her agreement, passed it on to Dr Haworth as our safeguarding lead. Her cervical screening was also overdue and has been rebooked for next month.

Kind regards

Joanne Pellow RGN
Practice Nurse
NMC PIN 08I4417E

Re: Ms Natalia KOWALCZYK (dob 19/11/1987)

1. Attendance
Ms Kowalczyk walked in to the UTC at approximately 19:30 on 23 September 2026. She was triaged and then seen by me in cubicle 4.

2. Examination
I examined her in person. Findings:
  a) periorbital bruising, left eye, appearing 1-2 days old
  b) a split to the lower lip, not needing closure
  c) an oval bruise on the right forearm with visible tooth impressions, consistent with a human bite
  d) two patches of hair loss at the crown, scalp tender to touch

X-ray of the right forearm was normal. The bite was cleaned and dressed and she was started on antibiotics.

3. History given
Ms Kowalczyk told me that her partner, Aaron Brooke, attacked her at home two days before, after an argument about money, and that he pulled her hair out and bit her arm when she tried to get past him to the front door.

4. Opinion
In my professional judgement her injuries, the bite mark and hair loss especially, are consistent with Ms Kowalczyk being a victim of domestic abuse. They are not the sort of injuries I would expect to see from an accident.

5. Other
She declined referral to the hospital safeguarding team on the day but did take the information leaflet. A copy of this letter has gone to her GP.

Yours sincerely

C. Malhotra

Coles Davenport LLP

Mrs Lorraine Pike, 9 Mardyke Terrace, Bristol BS3 4PQ - DOB 12.05.1979

Thank you for your letter. Mrs Pike has given her consent for me to reply.

I saw Mrs Pike in person at the surgery on 15 September 2026. On examination there was extensive bruising over the right hip and outer thigh, a bruise on the right forearm and tenderness over the right lower ribs, with no clinical sign of fracture. At that appointment she told me she had fallen off a stepladder while decorating the hall.

I understand she has since told our reception team that her husband, Gavin Pike, pushed her and that the stepladder account wasn't true.

You have asked me to confirm that her injuries are consistent with domestic abuse. I'm sorry, but I don't feel able to do that. The injuries I saw are entirely explained by the fall she described at the time, and nothing in my examination findings would let me tell a fall apart from a push or any other cause. I therefore cannot give an opinion one way or the other as to whether Mrs Pike's injuries are consistent with her being a victim of domestic abuse.

I have recorded her later account in her notes. If she would like to come in and talk things through she is welcome to book with me or one of my colleagues.

Please be aware the practice is closed for staff training on the afternoon of 14 October.

Yours sincerely

Dr Helen Marchetti
GP

From: Jordan Okonkwo-Reid <jordan.okonkwo-reid@northmercia-ambulance.nhs.uk>
To: Pelling & Co Solicitors <family@pellingco.co.uk>
Sent: 14 September 2026 09:12
Subject: Amira Hassan - your request re 999 attendance 27/08

Good morning,

Apologies for the delay. I've been on a run of nights and your request sat in the station inbox for a while before it got to me.

I'm a paramedic with North Mercia Ambulance Service NHS Trust, registered with the HCPC (registration no. PA48127). I have seen Ms Hassan's signed consent for me to write to you.

At about 00:50 on 27 August 2026 my crewmate and I were sent to Ms Amira Hassan's home after a neighbour rang 999 reporting screaming. Police arrived at the same time as us. I examined Ms Hassan in her kitchen and again in the back of the ambulance on the way to Birchfield General.

What I found:
* swelling and tenderness over the left cheekbone and jaw
* reddened marks across the front and sides of her neck, with pinpoint (petechial) haemorrhages around both eyes
* friction abrasions on both knees, of the type you see from being dragged across carpet
* hoarse voice; she said it hurt to swallow

She told me her husband, Faisal Hassan, had grabbed her round the throat and pulled her across the lounge floor by her hair.

My clinical view, based on that examination, is that her injuries are consistent with her being a victim of domestic abuse. The neck findings in particular are a pattern we're trained to treat as non-fatal strangulation and I can't think of an accidental explanation that would fit.

We handed her over to the ED team at 01:40. I don't have any information about her care after that.

Regards

Jordan Okonkwo-Reid
Paramedic | HCPC PA48127
North Mercia Ambulance Service NHS Trust - Hollybank Station
0121 496 0644

I am a registered midwife (NMC PIN 09J4471E) and have been Ms Okonjo's named community midwife since she booked with us in May. She is currently 31 weeks pregnant with her second baby.

Ms Okonjo attended a routine antenatal appointment with me at Fairfield Children's Centre on 15 September 2026. While I was palpating her abdomen I noticed bruising to both upper arms, in a pattern of four to five oval marks on the inner aspect of each arm, together with a healing graze along the left side of her jaw. When I asked her about these, and about her safety at home, she became tearful and did not want to go into detail. I examined her fully, recorded the injuries on a body map and documented them in both her handheld and electronic maternity notes. The baby's heart rate and growth were within normal limits.

I did consider other possible explanations. Based on my own examination, and on the distribution of the bruising, which has the appearance of grip marks, it is my professional judgement that Ms Okonjo's injuries are consistent with her being a victim of domestic abuse.

Since that appointment I have referred her to the hospital IDVA, informed our safeguarding midwife, and increased her antenatal contacts to fortnightly. She has also been given a direct number for the labour ward should she need to come in out of hours.

I hope this is of some assistance. I can be reached through the office number above, Monday to Friday; please note I am on leave from 6 to 17 October.

NORTHGATE COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH HUB
Adult Psychology Service
41 Tanner Street, Leeds LS9 7QD  |  0113 496 0255

PSYCHOLOGICAL ASSESSMENT - SUMMARY FOR LEGAL PURPOSES

Author: Dr Tomasz Wierzbicki, Consultant Clinical Psychologist
HCPC registration no.: PYL041876
Date of report: 2 October 2026

1. Client
1.1 Mrs Priya Lakshmi Varadarajan (DOB 09/08/1988), referred by her GP on 19 August 2026.

2. How I assessed her
2.1 I met Mrs Varadarajan on three occasions by secure video call, on 4, 11 and 25 September 2026, for roughly an hour each time. At the start of every session I checked that she was alone and able to speak freely.
2.2 Alongside clinical interview I administered the PCL-5 and PHQ-9.

3. Findings
3.1 She was visibly hypervigilant throughout, repeatedly checking the door behind her and startling at a phone notification. She described nightmares, avoidance of anything connected with the marital home, and a fixed expectation that she will be punished for small mistakes.
3.2 Her PCL-5 score of 58 is well above the threshold usually taken to indicate probable PTSD. PHQ-9 was 19.
3.3 She gave a history of her husband, Mr Arjun Varadarajan, controlling her access to money, going through her phone each night and threatening to send her back to her family "in disgrace".

4. Opinion
4.1 I have asked myself whether anything else in her history could account for this picture. There is no record of psychological difficulty before the marriage and no other trauma of comparable weight. I am satisfied that what she now suffers from is the kind of psychological injury that develops in a person subjected, over a long period, to coercive and controlling behaviour by a partner, and in my opinion that is by far its likeliest origin. Put simply, what I have seen fits with her having been abused.

5. Recomendations
5.1 Trauma-focused therapy is indicated. She has been placed on our waiting list, which currently stands at about 14 weeks.

Dr T. Wierzbicki

Dear Ms Ambrose,

Thank you for your letter of 21 September and the signed patient consent, which I have scanned onto the record.

By way of background, I am a GP partner at Holloway Lane Medical Practice. I was not the clinician who saw Ms Bostock on the occasion you ask about. She was examined face to face here on 3 March 2026 by Dr Simon Achebe, a locum who covered a number of sessions for us in the spring. Dr Achebe has since moved abroad to work and, despite trying both his last known email address and the locum agency, we have not been able to reach him, so he is not available to write this himself.

As a partner I have full access to Ms Bostock's medical records, including Dr Achebe's consultation entry. He recorded a tender, swollen left wrist, linear bruising to the left side of the neck and a split lower lip. Ms Bostock's account at the time was that her partner had pushed her against a kitchen worktop and held her by the throat. I have seen her twice myself since then on unrelated matters, which I haven't gone into here.

Calder Valley Primary Care Mental Health Service
Brook House, 6 Sowerby Road, Halifax HX6 2JL
Tel: 01632 960 587

23 September 2026

Dear Sir/Madam

Ms Farah Iqbal-Thornton

I write in support of Ms Iqbal-Thornton, who was referred to our service by her GP in July 2026.

I am a Senior Mental Health Practitioner with the service. I carried out Ms Iqbal-Thornton's initial assessment by telephone on 29 July and have since seen her for six one-to-one appointments, all held by video because she has not felt able to travel into town.

At assessment she presented with significant anxiety and low mood. She was sleeping no more than three or four hours a night, had lost weight and described being frightened to leave her flat in case she ran into her ex-husband, Mr Adam Thornton. She told me he has repeatedly waited outside her workplace and has sent messages threatening to "ruin" her and to tell her employer lies about her.

Across our appointments I have observed marked hypervigilance, tearfulness and avoidance; on two occasions she ended the call early after a knock at her door. In my professional judgement Ms Iqbal-Thornton's condition is consistent with her having been a victim of domestic abuse, and her symptoms are in keeping with what I would expect to see after a prolonged period of harassment and intimidation by a former partner.

She will remain open to our service until at least December, and we have discussed a referral to the local domestic abuse outreach team, which she is considering.

Yours faithfully

Joel Ashworth
Senior Mental Health Practitioner
Calder Valley Primary Care Mental Health Service

Refuge - Outreach - Children & Young People

25 September 2026

PRIVATE AND CONFIDENTIAL

To whom it may concern

Ms Charlotte Anne Bramwell, DOB 03/01/1991

Tynewell Women's Aid is a domestic abuse charity situated in Newcastle upon Tyne, in the United Kingdom. We provide refuge accommodation, community outreach and advocacy to women and children, and the charity has operated without interruption since 1998.

I am a Refuge Support Worker with nine years' experience in specialist domestic abuse services. I have been Ms Bramwell's keyworker since she moved into one of our refuge properties on 11 August 2026.

At her intake meeting, and in more detail since, Ms Bramwell told me that her partner, Mr Liam Tordoff:
  * took her bank card in early 2025 and from then on gave her £20 in cash a week;
  * locked her out of the house overnight in July 2026 with no shoes, coat or phone;
  * on 7 August 2026 pinned her to the kitchen floor by her throat and said he would kill her if she ever left.
We completed a DASH risk assessment with her on 11 August, which scored 17 (high risk), and referred her case to MARAC.

In my professional judgement Ms Bramwell is a victim of domestic abuse and remains at risk of further harm from Mr Tordoff.

She needed our help because she had to leave home at once, had no money of her own and nowhere to go where he would not find her. Since 11 August we have given her a refuge place for herself and her son, weekly one-to-one keywork, safety planning, help opening a bank account in her sole name and a referral to our children's worker. I also went with her to her homelessness appointment on 2 September.

Yours faithfully

Megan Thirlwell
Refuge Support Worker

From: Sasha Okafor-Brennan <s.okafor-brennan@harbourline.org.uk>

Subject: Ms Natalia Kowalczyk - supporting letter for LAA

Dear Matthew,

As requested, please treat this email as Harbourline's letter in support of Ms Natalia Kowalczyk.

About us: Harbourline Domestic Abuse Service is a registered charity based in Reading, Berkshire, UK. We provide Independent Domestic Violence Advisor (IDVA) support, outreach and a local helpline, and the charity has operated continuously since it was set up in March 2014.

About me: I'm a Senior IDVA, accredited in 2019, and I've been Ms Kowalczyk's allocated advisor since 24 August 2026 following a police referral.

What I've relied on: Ms Kowalczyk told me, and information shared with us through MARAC supports, that her ex-partner Mr Daniel Ferreira-Hale sent her more than 140 texts and voice notes between 10pm on 20 August and 3am the next morning; turned up at the dental surgery where she works on 21 August and refused to leave until staff called the police; slashed two of her car tyres; and on 22 August grabbed her by the hair on her doorstep and dragged her down the steps.

My professional judgement is that Ms Kowalczyk is a victim of domestic abuse and remains at high risk of serious harm from Mr Ferreira-Hale.

She needed support because the stalking was escalating quickly, he knows both her home and work addresses, and she was too frightened to sleep at home. Support given so far: risk assessment and safety plan (24/08); MARAC referral (heard 10/09); new locks and a video doorbell through the sanctuary scheme (fitted 03/09); liaison with the investigating officer about his bail conditions; and weekly phone check-ins, which are ongoing.

Regards,

Sasha Okafor-Brennan
Senior IDVA | Harbourline Domestic Abuse Service
0118 496 0742 | 07700 900316

From: Priti Sandhu <priti.sandhu@lanternnetwork.org>
To: enquiries@hollisrowe-solicitors.co.uk
Sent: 16 September 2026 14:58
Subject: Re: Letter of support - Roxanne Adebayo-Wilks

Good afternoon,

Further to your request of last week, I can confirm the following.

The Lantern Network is a specialist domestic abuse charity offering advocacy, emotional support and safety planning to survivors by telephone, video and live chat. We have been operating continuously, without any break in service, since we were founded in 2016.

I am an Advocacy Coordinator and have worked with Ms Roxanne Adebayo-Wilks since 29 June 2026, when she first contacted our chat service late at night from a friend's bathroom.

Ms Adebayo-Wilks has described to me how her husband, Mr Gareth Pellow, routinely took her car keys and phone so that she could not leave the house; made her account for everything she spent (she has sent us bank screenshots showing he moved her salary into his own account each month); and in June spat in her face and shoved her into a wardrobe in front of their daughter.

Based on what she has told me, the documents she has shared and my twelve years in this field, it is my professional judgement that she is a victim of domestic abuse and is at ongoing risk from Mr Pellow.

Ms Adebayo-Wilks needed support because she had no access to money or transport, felt unable to tell her family, and was thinking of going back to him as she could see no other way of keeping a roof over her daughter's head. Since 29 June we have provided fortnightly advocacy calls, a written safety plan, help completing her housing application and a referral to a refuge, which she took up in August.

Kind regards,

Priti Sandhu
Advocacy Coordinator
The Lantern Network
www.lanternnetwork.org

If you are worried about your safety while reading this, use the quick-exit button on our website.

Dear Mr Hussain,

Thanks for your call on Friday. I am a Tenancy Sustainment Officer in the Neighbourhoods and Tenancy Support team at Meridian Housing Association, and Ms Chantelle Anderson-Price's tenancy has been on my patch since 2023.

Since July this year we have had four reports from neighbours at Thornfield Court about shouting and banging from her flat late at night. When I visited on 12 August Ms Anderson-Price had a black eye and the bedroom door had been pulled off its hinges. She told me her ex-partner had done this after she refused to let him stay the night. On 20 August the block's CCTV showed him trying to force the communal entrance at about 2am, and he has since posted abusive messages about her on the residents' Facebook group.

In my professional judgement Ms Anderson-Price is a victim of domestic abuse and remains at risk from her ex-partner, who still knows where she lives.

As a result Meridian approved an emergency management transfer on 3 September, and she moved into a two-bedroom property in a different district on 22 September. We paid for the removal and have referred her to our floating support service, which starts next week.

If you need this on letterhead let me know and I'll get it signed off by my manager.

Best wishes,

Joanne Feltham

ROWAN CLOSE
women's support, east end
Scottish Charity No. SC041822
14 Gallowgate Lane, Glasgow G40 2TS  -  0141 496 0377

3rd October 2026

To whoever is reading this on Mrs McAllister's behalf,

I'd like to tell you a bit about Mrs Shona Kirsteen McAllister, and a bit about us.

Rowan Close is a small Scottish charity. We work out of one office, in the east end of Glasgow, and what we are for is helping women get clear of men who hurt and control them. Our doors have stayed open, without a single break, since the autumn of 2007 - through funding scares, a burst water main and the pandemic.

Shona came to us on 14 August with a carrier bag and a five-month-old baby. She had no money she could get at, no key to anywhere, and not one friend her husband didn't know about. That is why she needed us.

What she has told us, and what we have seen of the aftermath, includes this. Mr Darren McAllister kept her passport and emptied her wages out of her account on payday. He stood over her whenever she phoned her own mother. On the night of 2 August he put his fist through the bathroom door she had locked herself behind; she later showed our worker a photo of the hole.

I have done this work for nineteen years and I don't put things like this in writing unless I mean them. My honest professional view is that what has been done to Shona is domestic abuse, and that she is nowhere near safe from more of it.

Since the middle of August we have found her and the baby a bed in one of our safe flats, sat beside her through two police statements, sorted a crisis grant so there was a cot and food in the place, and our worker Elaine meets her every Tuesday without fail.

Morag Lennox
Service Manager

Unit 7, Kelham Works, Alma Street, Sheffield S3 8SA, UK  -  0114 496 0163

28 September 2026

Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Ms Bethany Rose Lindqvist

The Meadowlark Project is a community interest company situated in Sheffield in the United Kingdom. We offer one-to-one support, advocacy and a weekly drop-in for anyone affected by domestic abuse, and we have been operating continuously since we launched this summer. Our founder, Carol Mwangi, spent ten years as an IDVA with a regional charity before setting Meadowlark up.

I am a Domestic Abuse Support Worker and have supported Ms Lindqvist since 15 August 2026, when she self-referred at our drop-in.

Ms Lindqvist has told me that her partner, Mr Owen Pritchard, has repeatedly read her messages and demanded her passwords, refused to let her see friends unless he came too, and on 9 August pushed her down the last few stairs when she said she wanted to spend the weekend at her brother's. I saw the bruising to her hip and elbow myself when we first met.

In my professional judgement Ms Lindqvist is a victim of domestic abuse and remains at risk from Mr Pritchard.

She needed support because she had become very isolated, had started to believe she was to blame, and was frightened of how he would react if she ended the relationship. So far we have given her seven weekly one-to-one sessions, a written safety plan, help to find a solicitor, and practical support looking for a private rental away from the area, which is still ongoing.

Please contact me on the number above if you need anything else.

Yours faithfully,

Jade Okonkwo-Reid
Domestic Abuse Support Worker

St Aldric's Hospital (fictional), Emergency Department
Riverside Road, Anytown AN1 1AA
14 September 2026

To whom it may concern

Re: Ms J. Doe, date of birth 02/03/1990

I am an emergency medicine consultant registered with the General Medical Council (GMC number 0000000). I examined Ms Doe in person in this department on 12 September 2026.

On examination she had a large haematoma around the left eye, a fracture of the left ulna and fractures of two left ribs, confirmed on X-ray. On both forearms there were multiple small round scars of differing ages, in a pattern typical of cigarette burns, some recent and some several years old.

Ms Doe attended with her husband, who stayed in the cubicle. Before answering any question she looked at him first. Her pupils were dilated. She flinched each time he moved. When I asked how the injuries happened, she said she had fallen, that she was clumsy and always falling, while looking at her husband throughout.

I asked her husband to leave the cubicle to complete some paperwork at reception. Once he had gone, I told Ms Doe that we could keep her safe but that I needed her to tell me the truth. I asked whether the man who had come in with her had caused these injuries. She nodded.

Yours faithfully,

Dr S. Okafor (fictional), MBBS FRCEM Consultant in Emergency Medicine
